claims: The Artemis II mission is scheduled to launch on April 1, 2026.
The Artemis II mission is scheduled to launch at 6:35 p.m. EDT.
The Artemis II mission has a launch window from 5:24–7:24 pm CT.
The Artemis II mission is scheduled to launch from Kennedy Space Center, FL.
The Artemis II mission is a 10-day mission.
The Artemis II mission will take four astronauts.
The Artemis II mission is a crewed flyby around the Moon.
The Artemis II mission marks the first human return to deep space since 1972.
The Artemis II mission liftoff is on the SLS rocket.
The Artemis II mission's Initial Orbit is April 1–2.
During the Artemis II mission's Initial Orbit, the crew tests Orion capsule systems in high Earth orbit.
The Artemis II mission's Translunar Injection is April 2.
During the Artemis II mission's Translunar Injection, there is an engine firing to leave Earth orbit for the Moon.
The Artemis II mission's Lunar Flyby is April 6.
The Artemis II mission's Lunar Flyby is the closest approach to the Moon on Day 6.
The Artemis II mission's Return & Splashdown is April 10.
During the Artemis II mission's Return & Splashdown, there is re-entry and landing in the Pacific Ocean.
Backup launch dates for the Artemis II mission are available on April 2-6 and April 30.
